author: 132ikl
body:
# Description

I was reading through the documentation yesterday, when I stumbled upon [this section](https://www.nushell.sh/book/pipelines.html#behind-the-scenes) explaining how command output is formatted using the `table` command. I was surprised that this section didn't mention the `display_output` hook, so I took a look in the code and was shocked to discovered that the documentation was correct, and the `table` command _is_ automatically applied to printed pipelines.

This auto-tabling has two ramifications for the `display_output` hook:

1. The `table` command is called on the output of a pipeline after the `display_output` has run, even if `display_output` contains the table command. This means each pipeline output is roughly equivalent to the following (using `ls` as an example): 
    ```nushell
    ls | do $config.hooks.display_output | table
    ```
2. If `display_output` returns structured data, it will _still_ be formatted through the table command.

This PR removes the auto-table when the `display_output` hook is set. The auto-table made sense before `display_output` was introduced, but to me, it now seems like unnecessary "automagic" which can be accomplished using existing Nushell features.

This means that you can now pull back the curtain a bit, and replace your `display_output` hook with an empty closure (`$env.config.hooks.display_output = {||}`, setting it to null retains the previous behavior) to see the values printed normally without the table formatting. I think this is a good thing, and makes it easier to understand Nushell fundamentals.

It is important to note that this PR does not change how `print` and other commands (well, specifically only `watch`) print out values. They continue to use `table` with no arguments, so changing your config/`display_output` hook won't affect what `print`ing a value does.

Rel: [Discord discussion](https://discord.com/channels/601130461678272522/615329862395101194/1307102690848931904) (cc @dcarosone)

# User-Facing Changes
<!-- List of all changes that impact the user experience here. This helps us keep track of breaking changes. -->

Pipelines are no longer automatically formatted using the `table` command. Instead, the `display_output` hook is used to format pipeline output. Most users should see no impact, as the default `display_output` hook already uses the `table` command.

# Tests + Formatting
<!--
Don't forget to add tests that cover your changes.

Make sure you've run and fixed any issues with these commands:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` to check standard code formatting (`cargo fmt --all` applies these changes)
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used` to check that you're using the standard code style
- `cargo test --workspace` to check that all tests pass (on Windows make sure to [enable developer mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/get-started/developer-mode-features-and-debugging))
- `cargo run -- -c "use toolkit.nu; toolkit test stdlib"` to run the tests for the standard library

> **Note**
> from `nushell` you can also use the `toolkit` as follows
> ```bash
> use toolkit.nu  # or use an `env_change` hook to activate it automatically
> toolkit check pr
> ```
-->

- :green_circle: `toolkit fmt`
- :green_circle: `toolkit clippy`
- :green_circle: `toolkit test`
- :green_circle: `toolkit test stdlib`

# After Submitting
<!-- If your PR had any user-facing changes, update [the documentation](https://github.com/nushell/nushell.github.io) after the PR is merged, if necessary. This will help us keep the docs up to date. -->

Will update mentioned docs page to call out `display_output` hook.

author: 3-w-c
body:
Currently, after working on a few different activities in a day, the "daily summary" expands in width, pushing the start of the activity field off the screen.

This PR adds a dconf-only option (no UI yet) to hide the activity completely, to work around this issue.

A better fix might be to make the summary flow onto multiple lines; I went with an option to hide it instead because it seemed easier – and I'm fine launching hamster if I want to see the summary.

author: legendnt1
body:
This pull request includes several changes to the `MiFarma` project, focusing on refactoring sorting functions and modifying methods to handle product counts in the shopping cart. The most important changes include removing redundant sorting functions, updating sorting logic in `VistaEmpleado`, and enhancing the `VistaUsuario` class to manage product counts more effectively.

Refactoring sorting functions:

* Removed the `ordenarUsuarioxEdad` function, which called `mergeSort`, from `Funciones.h` as it was redundant.
* Removed the `ordenarXPrecio` function, which called `quickSort`, from `Funciones.h` for the same reason.

Updating sorting logic:

* Updated the `VistaEmpleado` class to use `quickSort` directly instead of the `ordShellProductoMenorAMayor` function for sorting products.

Enhancing product count management:

* Modified the `VistaUsuario` class to include the `cont_productos_comprados` parameter in the `verCarrito` and `eliminarTodoCarrito` methods to keep track of the number of products in the cart. author: aralroca
body:
Fixes https://github.com/brisa-build/brisa/issues/118
Related https://github.com/brisa-build/brisa/issues/628 (first step)
Related https://github.com/brisa-build/brisa/issues/556 (first step)
Related https://github.com/brisa-build/brisa/issues/470 (first step)

In this PR I have changed:

- I've made the transpilation part of the actions to be during the first build instead of a second build.
- I've removed the plugin usage in the second build since it is done in a previous process.
- Now the actions are bundled in a single file, which will allow later to make the change of build strategy that we plan to do to improve req/sec and change the import dynamic by a static in build-time (this will be done in another PR, but it is already aligned to be done).
- The ids of the actions are now deterministic, so it avoids bugs with the hot-reload. Instead of using an incremental number, which paths during build concurrency can change order, and was the bug of conflicts during hot-reload, they now keep an id based on a hash of the filename.

**Before**:

![process](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94d79ee6-418c-4b93-89a1-9d2bd893bfa0)

**Now**:

![now_process](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e9107f4-7372-4203-9323-90c39b8a4878)

**Future _(next PRs, but we have some blocks from new Bun APIs that are coming soon)_**:

- Reduce to 2 builds (server + client) even if there are 100 or more pages.

The multi-build of the current client pages is as workaround because IIFE was not supported in Bun. We need it to make the pages interactive during HTML streaming. But now Bun has supported IIFE, although it is experimental and there is no documentation yet, but this will probably improve build times considerably.

author: numpsy
body:
A thought whilst we're open for API changes:

As it stands, for each entry in the property name dictionary, DictionaryProperty 
- creates a new instance of DictionaryEntry
- calls the Read function, which stores the bytes for the entry
- reads the Name property, which decodes the stored bytes and returns the string
- discards the DictionaryEntry

This seems a bit round about to me for what it's doing, so I propose just doing a simple inline read and not having an instanced DictionaryEntry class.

This also makes it easier to see if the ReadBytes calls could be changed to Read or merged together and and then sliced with spans later.

body:
# Description

Fetch all jobs available when page loads from database to display along with images 
Clicking on a job posting should take the user to the specific job link which means it displays the details of the job and link to form to apply

Please test the following API endpoints to ensure they function as expected. Use appropriate HTTP methods for each endpoint and provide necessary request data for testing:

GET /: Retrieves a list of all available jobs.
GET /:id: Retrieves the details of a specific job by its unique ID.
POST /: Creates a new job entry. Provide relevant job details in the request body.
PUT /:id: Updates an existing job by its unique ID. Include updated job details in the request body.
DELETE /:id: Deletes a specific job by its unique ID.
Feel free to provide feedback on any bugs, issues, or improvements related to the endpoints.

author: tradestreamhq
body:
This pull request introduces a new `CandleManager` interface and updates the existing `CandleManagerImpl` to implement it, enhancing modularity and flexibility in the trade processing pipeline. The following changes are included:  

### Changes:
1. **New Interface: `CandleManager`**  
   - Defines the contract for managing and processing trade data:
     - `processTrade(Trade trade)`: Processes individual trades.
     - `handleThinlyTradedMarkets(List<String> currencyPairs)`: Handles scenarios for markets with low trading volume.

2. **Implementation: `CandleManagerImpl`**  
   - Updated `CandleManagerImpl` to implement the `CandleManager` interface.
   - Retains existing functionality with added structure for adherence to the new interface.

3. **Build Configuration Updates:**  
   - Added a new `java_library` rule for `candle_manager` in the `BUILD` file.
   - Updated `candle_manager_impl` dependencies to include `candle_manager`.

### Key Benefits:
- Establishes a clear separation of concerns with an interface to define the high-level responsibilities of a `CandleManager`.
- Enhances testability and future scalability by providing a contract (`CandleManager`) for alternate implementations.
- Ensures better management of thinly traded markets, improving trade data aggregation.

### Notes:
- `handleThinlyTradedMarkets` currently accepts a list of currency pairs but can be extended for additional parameters as needed.
- Further improvements could include metrics tracking for candle creation and market activity monitoring. 

This update sets the stage for more robust and adaptable trade ingestion and management.
